payload.title: Australia Real Weddings From Coast to Country

payload.excerpt: These 12 Australia real wedding stories are grouped by the setting each couple chose: a clifftop, a vineyard, a city room, a garden or an island. Each card links to the couple's full story.
key_takeaways: Every wedding below comes from our own published stories, grouped into coast and beach, country and vineyard, city, garden and island settings, and linked to the couple's full account.
Before you book an Australian venue, ask where an outdoor ceremony moves if the weather turns and who makes that call on the day.
To marry legally in Australia, you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
What these couples share becomes a set of questions for any Australian venue, from guests travelling in to a route without steps for older guests.

faq.q: Where can we read more real weddings held in Australia?
faq.a: Each card above links to the couple's full story, and our real weddings hub carries couples from Australia and beyond. For settings and ideas from couples around the world, see [wedding inspiration from real couples around the world](/real-weddings/where-do-you-find-real-wedding-inspiration).

faq.q: Can we marry legally in Australia if we live overseas?
faq.a: Yes. The Notice of Intended Marriage can be completed from overseas, and it still goes to an authorised marriage celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

faq.q: Who can legally marry us in Australia?
faq.a: An authorised marriage celebrant: a Commonwealth-registered celebrant, a Commonwealth-registered religious celebrant, a minister of religion from a recognised denomination, or a state or territory officer.

faq.q: When should we lodge our Notice of Intended Marriage?
faq.a: At least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. If the date is closer than 1 month, talk to your celebrant, since a prescribed authority may approve the marriage going ahead.

faq.q: What should we ask an Australian venue about the weather?
faq.a: Ask where the covered option is and whether it seats every guest, who decides on the move and how many hours ahead, and what shade sits over the ceremony seating at the hour you marry.

cta.subtext: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as your single point of contact.
